Fort Worth Bathroom Remodeling: From First Visit to Final Walkthrough Bathroom remodels are easier to manage when the first visit answers the real questions, not just the style ones. Fort Worth bathroom remodeling should start with the home itself: site access, parking, measurements, plumbing location, ventilation, lighting, fixture spacing, storage, household disruption, and the age or style of the property. Those early details can shape scheduling, trade coordination, material choices, and whether the project stays clear once work begins. At Amour Remodeling DFW, we help homeowners connect the in-home consultation to a realistic scope, written expectations, and a process that stays understandable from planning through final walkthrough. A stronger project-prep step can help with: Cleaner access and timing conversations Fewer change orders during renovation Better fixture, tile, and storage decisions Less disruption to daily routines A bathroom plan built around the actual home Schedule an in-home consultation with Amour before the project starts.

Our latest case study highlights a complete tub-to-shower conversion we completed for Devares and Sandy in Mount Holly, NC. For Devares and Sandy, their traditional bathtub was no longer serving their needs. High tub walls can make stepping in and out difficult, and an unused tub simply takes up valuable space. They wanted a modernized wet area that prioritized both accessibility and contemporary design. Our team removed their old bathtub and replaced it with a stunning, spacious walk-in shower. The new layout eliminates the high barrier, providing a seamless and much safer entry. Not only does this tub-to-shower conversion drastically improve the accessibility of their bathroom, but it also opens up the room, making it feel larger and more inviting. The new shower features premium, low-maintenance materials that resist mold and mildew, giving Devares and Sandy a fresh, beautiful space that requires minimal upkeep. By focusing on smart design, we delivered a completely transformed shower area with minimal disruption to their home. This laundry room in Placerville shows a full cabinet build above and around the washer and dryer. The upper cabinets run wall to wall above the machines, and a base cabinet with a tall storage unit on the right side adds covered storage without taking up floor space in the middle of the room. Laundry rooms are often treated as afterthoughts when it comes to storage, but a cabinet build like this one turns the room into a functional space with a place for everything. The oak doors here tie into the style of the rest of the home rather than looking like utility shelving added after the fact. Getting the cabinet height right above a top-load or front-load machine matters. Upper cabinets set too low restrict access to the machine controls and the drum, so the clearance has to be planned around the specific appliances before anything is built. Pro Tip: Before planning laundry room cabinets, measure the height of your machines with the lid or door fully open. That measurement sets the minimum clearance for the bottom of any upper cabinet above them.

From the owner
Livermore Fall Evenings Deserve a Better Deck The heat finally breaks. Golden light stretches across the valley, the air smells like harvest season, and by six o'clock it is the kind of evening that belongs outside. In Livermore, fall might be the best season of the whole year for the backyard, as long as the backyard is ready for it. Too many outdoor spaces fall short at exactly this moment. The deck is too small for a table and a few chairs. The stairs feel wobbly. There is no shade for sunny afternoons and nowhere comfortable to linger after the sun drops behind the hills. A well-planned deck changes how a household uses the whole property. Think of a wider platform that fits a real dining table, a step-down lounge area, built-in benches that double as storage, and railings that frame the view instead of blocking it. Paired with the right materials, it becomes an extension of the living room for many months each year. Partners Remodeling designs and builds decks, fencing and outdoor living spaces in Livermore, Pleasanton, Dublin and across the Tri-Valley. Planning now also gives you time to design, permit and build before next spring rolls around. We are family-owned, licensed, bonded and insured, with a warranty on labor and materials. Request a free outdoor consultation through our Google profile.

From the owner
Custom kitchen cabinets can transform how a kitchen looks and functions. Unlike stock options, custom cabinetry is built around your exact space, style, and storage needs. Cutting Edge Contractors designs and crafts custom kitchen cabinets for homeowners in Bonita Springs, Bonita Bay, Estero, and North Naples. Well-designed cabinetry does more than store dishes. It sets the tone for the entire kitchen and makes daily routines easier. We plan every detail, including layout, materials, hardware, and finishes, so the cabinets fit your kitchen and your lifestyle. Soft-close hardware, smart interior storage, and durable materials suited to the Southwest Florida climate are all part of the process. Because custom cabinets are often the centerpiece of a kitchen remodel, we integrate them into the larger design from the start. Using LiDAR scanning and photo-realistic 3D renders, we show you how the finished cabinetry will look in your space before anything is built. You receive a fixed-price contract and a clear plan from a licensed, insured contractor. Whether you are remodeling an entire kitchen or focusing on cabinetry alone, thoughtful custom cabinets are a lasting upgrade. A planning session is a simple way to review styles, layouts, and options, and to see how custom cabinets can improve the way your Bonita Springs kitchen works.

From the owner
Finish or Remodel Your Basement? Know the Difference Thinking about the basement this winter? Homeowners often ask us whether they need a basement finish or a basement remodel. The two sound alike, but they start from different places, and we just added a plain-English explanation to our basement finishing page. Finishing turns bare foundation walls and open joists into living space: framing, insulation, wiring, ductwork, drywall, ceilings and flooring. Remodeling reworks a basement someone finished years ago, which usually begins with tear-out and often turns up moisture or dated wiring the old finish was hiding. Either way, the work goes through the City's permit and inspection process. You also do not have to do the whole floor. Finishing a single room, such as a bedroom, office, gym or media room, is a project we build often, and a well-planned first room leaves space for a second phase later. The page also answers three new questions: what is included when we finish a basement, whether a general contractor or a basement specialist makes more sense, and how a one-room finish works. If you are in DuPage, Will or Kane County, take a look, then reach out for a free estimate. We will check for moisture on the first visit and tell you plainly what your basement needs.

From the owner
For a full home remodel, the design on paper only matters if the contractor can build it the way it was drawn. In Los Angeles, that makes the contractor’s relationship with the design a good way to judge them. Look at finished work up close. Photos hide a lot. Check tile lines, cabinet fit, trim, and paint edges in person or ask for references who will show you. Clean details at this scale usually mean a careful crew. Ask how selections are handled. Cabinets, tile, fixtures, and windows have lead times, and a good contractor has a system for choosing, ordering, and tracking them so the schedule doesn’t stall waiting on a missing item. Ask how they work with designers. Questions about layout, materials, and field changes come up constantly, and the contractor should be comfortable raising them early and not improvising on site. Ask how problems get reported. Surprises behind walls are normal, so you want clear communication, written change orders, and no silent substitutions. Confirm the basics yourself: license, insurance, and a written contract that spells out scope and payments. Call us today to talk through your full home remodel in Los Angeles.

From the owner
The fastest way to ruin a custom bath renovation is guessing what sits behind the drywall. Water leaks show up silently around plumbing fixtures, subfloors soften, and framing shifts out of square over time. When a contractor brings in hired day labor to hide damaged wood beneath new tile, you end up paying for a second remodel within two years. Solid carpentry is the foundation of every long-lasting bathroom remodel. Here is how our team approaches the work in Pinehurst, Southern Pines, and Hope Mills: Direct inspection down to the studs: We do not tile over compromised wood. Our full-time carpenters inspect the subfloor, sister weak joists, and rebuild studs so walls sit dead plumb before backer board ever touches the room. Built-in storage that stays square: Custom recessed niches and linen cabinets require exact framing. Because our in-house team cuts and builds the structure directly, the finish woodwork aligns clean against your tile lines. Clear communication from one crew: You speak with the same craftsmen who handle your framing and finish details. Daily project updates keep you informed without having to chase down separate trades. Building your space right from the studs forward protects your home and keeps your investment solid. #BathroomRemodel #CustomCarpentry

From the owner
A finished basement is only as secure as the waterproofing systems protecting it. When transforming a lower level into a luxurious living space, homeowners often want to completely hide their essential utility equipment behind drywall or inside custom cabinetry. However, failing to provide immediate, unrestricted access to your sump pump pit is a critical design error that can lead to catastrophic flooding. For basement remodeling projects in Voorhees, Marlton, and Cherry Hill, intelligent utility and mechanical planning must prioritize emergency access. A sump pump requires routine maintenance, including clearing the intake screen of debris and testing the float switch, to ensure it activates instantly during a heavy rainstorm. If the pump fails and is buried beneath heavy furniture or trapped behind a permanently screwed-in access panel, the delay in reaching the equipment will allow rising groundwater to destroy your new luxury vinyl floors and freshly painted drywall. We design sophisticated, seamlessly integrated utility closets and discrete floor hatches that keep the mechanicals completely out of sight during daily life, yet instantly accessible for maintenance or emergency replacement. Smart design protects your investment from the ground up. Call to discuss incorporating safe utility planning into your basement finishing design.

From the owner
Moving plumbing during a kitchen remodel can be a smart choice when it creates a more functional layout, improves workflow, or makes better use of valuable space. 🚰 Relocating a sink, dishwasher, or refrigerator water line requires more than simply extending a pipe; drain routing, venting, access, foundation type, cabinet placement, electrical connections, and appliance specifications all need to work together. A sink moved to a kitchen island, for example, may require careful planning beneath the floor, while a concrete slab can make drain relocation more involved and potentially more invasive. The best time to make these decisions is during the design stage, before cabinets are ordered and before rough plumbing begins, so the finished kitchen is built around a coordinated plan rather than costly last-minute changes—contact a qualified remodeling professional today to discuss your layout and determine whether moving your kitchen plumbing is worth the investment! 🛠️

The best pool design for a Huntington Beach backyard depends less on trends and more on how your specific space and lifestyle actually work. Lap pools suit narrow lots well. If your yard is long and tight rather than wide, a lap pool makes use of the space without forcing an awkward shape into a tricky footprint. Freeform pools work best when the yard has room to spare. Curved edges and natural shapes create a resort feel, but they need more square footage to look intentional rather than cramped. Plunge pools fit smaller coastal lots particularly well. Compact by design, they still deliver the cooling relief and visual impact of a full pool without demanding a large yard. Pools with integrated spas make sense for year round use here, since Huntington Beach's mild climate means a spa gets used even outside of pure summer months. The right design ultimately comes down to your lot's actual shape and how you plan to use the space, not just what looks best in a photo.
